Subject: Follow-up: discovery + recommended models / next steps

Hi Jared & Priya,

Great to meet this morning — thanks for walking through your search/NER use case and the scale constraints. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment: 

- What we heard: high-precision entity extraction from user queries (50K QPS monthly peak, burst to 120K/day), need for predictable latency (<120ms P95), and strict PII controls.
- Recommended model(s): redwood-turbo-1.6 (balanced quality/latency) and redwood-turbo-quant-1.6 (cost-optimized; slightly lower recall on low-frequency entities). I recommend starting the pilot on redwood-turbo-1.6.
- Eval artifacts: attached is a prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.txt) and our benchmark run for a comparable workload. Full eval dashboard here: https://doc.redwood.ai/evals/ACME-2026-01
- Quality guardrails: we can pin a specific model version for your account to avoid unexpected drift during model updates. I strongly recommend pinning for the pilot.

Proposed next steps:
1) Approve pilot scope (2 weeks, 100K monthly tokens / inference) — I can send an MOU.
2) I'll provision a pinned model for the pilot and share a short mutual action plan (MAP).
3) We'll run the benchmark/QA with your sample prompts and agree on acceptance criteria (F1 threshold for NER).

I've attached the prompt set and a recent benchmark snapshot for reference. Let me know if you want a live walkthrough of the eval dashboard this week — I have availability Thu/Fri afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
--

Thanks Marissa — the recap helps. A couple quick clarifications:

- On entity extraction: can you share precision/recall tradeoffs for low-frequency SKUs? Our priority is precision for downstream inventory routing.
- For pinning: how disruptive is it to our latency SLO if we pin a non-quantized version?

We're keen to start a pilot next week if we can get a clear acceptance test. Also, we noticed one of our environments auto-updated a hosted model yesterday (not from our side) — does Redwood perform rolling updates on hosted model variants by default? If so, that makes the pin suggestion critical.

—Jared

Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery + recommended models / next steps

Good questions — quick answers:

- Low-frequency SKU performance: in our benchmark (attached CSV) redwood-turbo-1.6 maintains ~0.78 F1 on the sparse-entity slice vs 0.71 for the quantized variant. We'll provide the per-entity breakdown in the pilot report.
- Latency: pinning a model version does not change the runtime path — you'll see identical latency characteristics for the same model binary. Pinning simply prevents automatic rolling updates to a newer model version for your tenancy.
- Rolling updates: for hosted customers who do not pin, we occasionally promote new model versions to our default catalog to pick up fixes and improvements. That said, we respect pinned versions and also provide an ops path for emergency rollbacks.

I've attached acme_prompt_set_v1.txt and benchmark_results_acme_v1_vs_v1.7.0.csv.

If you're good with pilot scope, I'll draft the MAP and request a pin for the pilot environment so you don't see catalog updates.

Best,
Marissa
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Thompson <jared@acme-retail.com>, nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery + recommended models / next steps

Marissa — following up with something urgent. After your message this morning we checked our staging results and observed a noticeable quality regression starting at ~02:00 AM PT (likely when the hosted catalog picked up v1.7.0). Example: our NER pipeline precision dropped for product_code entities; attached are 3 failing examples.

Quote (from our logs):
> Input: "Looking for SKU BLU-327-XL in Chicago store"
> Expected entities: product_code="BLU-327-XL"
> Model v1.6.3 output: product_code="BLU-327-XL" (ok)
> Model v1.7.0 output: product_code="BLU-327" (truncated, wrong)

This is blocking our ability to run the pilot — can you confirm whether ACME's hosted traffic was switched to v1.7.0, and if so can you pin us back to v1.6.3 or roll back the change? We need a short SLA on remediation for this regression.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior ML Engineer, ACME Retail

Fwd'ing Priya's note — ACME saw a regression after what looks like an auto-promotion to model v1.7.0. Per my earlier recommendation, they had not been pinned and so picked up the catalog change. They are asking for an immediate pin back to v1.6.3 or a rollback.

Attachments: prompt set and benchmark CSV (attached previously). Also attaching the failing examples sent by ACME.

As next steps: can Eng triage whether the delta between v1.6.3 -> v1.7.0 explains the truncation behavior Priya pasted? If so, please produce a diff report and either pin their tenancy to 1.6.3 (fast) or roll back the hosted variant (if multiple customers are impacted). ACME is asking for an SLA on remediation — please advise ETA so I can update them.

Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks for the heads up — looping in Eng ops. Quick update & plan: 

1) Immediate action: we will pin ACME's hosted tenancy to model version v1.6.3 within the hour to prevent further drift. This is non-disruptive and reversible.
2) Investigation: I'll run an automated diff between v1.6.3 and v1.7.0 using the ACME prompt set and your failing examples. Expect a preliminary diff report within 90 minutes. Output will include per-entity precision/recall deltas and tokenization-level diffs. (I'll post model_diff_v1.6.3_to_v1.7.0.txt to the eval link.)
3) Rollback decision: if the diff confirms a regression impacting ACME's acceptance criteria, we will coordinate a rollback of the hosted default for the affected variant. A rollback (catalog-level) will be scheduled with a short maintenance window; I'll confirm timing once we have the diff.

Can ACME share 10-20 additional failing examples (random sample) and any acceptance thresholds you want enforced? Jared/Priya — if you can drop examples into the shared Drive link, I'll pick them up immediately.

We'll keep communication tight — ETA: pin complete by ~16:00 PT, diff posted by ~16:30 PT.

—Vivek
